facts.fact_text: On 27 March 2008 the first applicant participated in a public gathering in the Stefan cel Mare park in Chișinău on the occasion of the anniversary of the 1918 reunification of Bessarabia with Romania.

On 27 March 2008 the fourth applicant participated in a public gathering in the Stefan cel Mare park in Chișinău on the occasion of the anniversary of the 1918 reunification of Bessarabia with Romania.
The demonstration held on 27 March 2008 in the Stefan cel Mare park in Chișinău had been authorised by the Chișinău Municipality.
At approximately 11.30 a.m. on 27 March 2008 the first and fourth applicants were arrested.
The Chișinău Court of Appeal concluded that the applicants' demonstration on 30 April 2008 had been peaceful.
At approximately 11.30 a.m. on 27 March 2008 the first and fourth applicants were arrested.
At the police station on 27 March 2008, the first and fourth applicants were charged with resisting arrest.
At the police station on 27 March 2008, the first and fourth applicants were charged with insulting police officers.
The first and fourth applicants were released several hours after their arrest on 27 March 2008.
On 26 May 2008 the Buiucani District Court finally acquitted the applicants of all charges arising from the events of 27 March 2008 in view of a lack of evidence against them.
On an unspecified date one of the applicants lodged a criminal complaint against the police officers who had arrested the applicants on 27 March 2008.
On 30 May 2008 the criminal complaint lodged against the police officers who had arrested the applicants on 27 March 2008 was dismissed as manifestly ill-founded.
After a short time during the demonstration on 22 April 2008, the first, second and fourth applicants were approached by several police officers who ordered them to leave.
The first, second and fourth applicants were arrested during the demonstration on 22 April 2008 in front of the residence of the President of Moldova.
The first, second and fourth applicants were charged with the offence of holding an unauthorised demonstration following their arrest on 22 April 2008.
The first, second and fourth applicants were charged with the offence of resisting arrest following their arrest on 22 April 2008.
The first, second and fourth applicants were charged with the offence of insulting police officers following their arrest on 22 April 2008.

On 8 May 2008 the Buiucani District Court acquitted the first, second and fourth applicants of all charges arising from the events of 22 April 2008 in view of a lack of incriminating evidence against them.

The Buiucani District Court found that the charges concerning resisting police officers brought against the first, second and fourth applicants in connection with the events of 22 April 2008 were groundless.

The Buiucani District Court found that the charges concerning insulting police officers brought against the first, second and fourth applicants in connection with the events of 22 April 2008 were groundless.
On an unspecified date the applicants lodged a criminal complaint against the police officers who had arrested them on 22 April 2008.
The criminal complaint lodged against the police officers who had arrested the applicants on 22 April 2008 was dismissed as manifestly ill-founded.

Article 40 of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that all meetings, demonstrations, rallies, processions or any other assemblies are free, but they may be organised and take place only peacefully and without the use of weapons.

Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and the protection of participants and the environment must be ensured, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic or the operation of businesses, and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering public order or the physical integrity or life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances including: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; and acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of public authorities, local authorities, prosecutors' offices, courts or companies with armed security.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the Parliament building, the residence of the President of Moldova, the seat of the Government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.
Section 8(4) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that free access to the premises of the institutions listed in section 8(3) shall be guaranteed.
Section 8(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local public authorities may, if the organisers agree, establish places or buildings for permanent assemblies.
Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council.

Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate: the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly; the date, starting time and finishing time; the location and access and return routes; the manner in which the assembly is to take place; the approximate number of participants; the persons responsible for the proper conduct of the assembly; and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.

Section 11(3) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that if the situation so requires, the Municipal Council may alter certain aspects of the prior notification with the agreement of the organiser of the assembly.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest five days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities may reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after consulting the police, they have obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting an application to hold an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, containing reasons for the refusal to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly may challenge the refusal in the administrative courts.

Section 19 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that participants in the assembly are required to respect the Act and other laws referred to therein, to respect the instructions of the organiser of the assembly and decisions of the municipality or police, and to leave the assembly if asked by the organiser, the municipality or the police.
On 22 February 2008 the Parliament of Moldova adopted a new Assemblies Act under which no authorisation was needed for the holding of demonstrations with less than fifty participants.

Article 166(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that illegal deprivation of liberty, other than kidnapping, shall be punishable by 120-240 hours of community work or imprisonment for up to two years.

Article 166(2) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that the same offence of illegal deprivation of liberty committed against two or more persons or by two or more persons shall be punishable by imprisonment for three to eight years.

Article 184(1) of the Criminal Code of Moldova provides that violation of the right to freedom of assembly by way of the illegal hindering of a demonstration, rally or act of protest, or the preventing of persons from taking part in them, when committed by an official, by two or more persons, or accompanied by acts of violence which do not pose a danger to life or health, shall be punishable by a fine of four to eight thousand Moldovan lei or by community work of 180-240 hours, or by imprisonment for up to two years.

Article 174 § 1(2) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that the organisation and holding of an assembly without prior notification of the Municipal Council or without authorisation from the Council, or in breach of the conditions concerning the conduct of meetings indicated in the authorisation, shall be punishable by a fine imposed on the organisers in an amount equal to between MDL 500 and 1,000.

Article 174 § 1(4) of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that active participation in an unauthorised assembly shall be punishable by a fine in an amount between MDL 200 and 300.

Article 174 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that resisting a police officer in the exercise of his or her duties of ensuring public order and the fight against crime shall be punishable by a fine of up to MDL 300 or detention for up to thirty days.

Article 174 § 6 of the Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that insulting police officers in the exercise of their duties shall be punishable by a fine of up to MDL 200 or imprisonment for up to fifteen days.

Article 249 of the Code of Administrative Offences provides that persons who disobey in bad faith the lawful orders of police officers, or resist or insult police officers, may be detained until their case is examined by a court.
